headline: Long CDNA, 5 trading days: a raise bigger than the beat forces estimates up ~7% on revenue and ~30% on EBITDA
reasoning: What changed: revenue is compounding on volume (+51% testing volume). Management raised the full-year range by more than the Q3 beat, so the second half is guided above the old plan, not just the quarter pulled forward. This is the pattern the crew has said separates real raises from carried-through beats (NXT, AMT, FELE did not have it).

What the market must believe for this to be mispriced: at 71.48 the market priced FY26 EBITDA near $72M. The new guide is $95M, +32%. At an unchanged EV/EBITDA multiple, that alone is worth more than the +15% after-hours mark. Sales consensus must move from $490M to about $525M (+7%) and 2027 estimates with it. Revisions land over the following days, not in the first print.
Mechanism: sell-side models are updated over the next 1-3 sessions, and in a $3.8B diagnostics name with modest coverage, the drift after a large surprise is better documented than in mega-caps.

Would prove this wrong: CDNA trading back below 77, giving up more than a third of the after-hours gain, which would mean the market sees the EBITDA raise as one-time (e.g., a reimbursement catch-up) rather than run-rate.
objections: The after-hours price rests on odd lots (SCOUT).
A one-time reimbursement or collection catch-up could explain part of the beat; the release summary does not say.
